title: UP BOARD CLASS 8 — English | Tenses Present Past Future
description: Subject-wise test on Tenses Present Past Future (English) for UP BOARD CLASS 8. 25Q.
subject: upbo8-english

questions.question: The Earth ______ around the Sun.

options.explanation: Incorrect tense for a general truth.
Correct tense for a general truth.
Present Continuous is not used for general truths.
Future tense is not used for general truths.

questions.explanation: This is a universal truth, which is expressed using the Simple Present Tense.
questions.hint: Use the verb form that describes a general truth.
questions.subject: upbo8-english

questions.question: My brother ______ his bicycle yesterday evening.

options.explanation: Present tense is incorrect for past actions.
Correct past tense form.
Future tense is incorrect for past actions.
Present Continuous is incorrect for past actions.

questions.explanation: The phrase 'yesterday evening' indicates a completed action in the past, requiring the Simple Past Tense.
questions.hint: Use the past tense form of the verb.
questions.subject: upbo8-english

questions.question: We ______ a new movie at the cinema next Friday.

options.explanation: Present tense is incorrect for future actions.
Past tense is incorrect for future actions.
Correct future tense form.
Present Continuous is incorrect for future actions.

questions.explanation: 'Next Friday' clearly indicates a future action, making the Simple Future Tense (will watch) the correct choice.
questions.hint: Use the future tense form of the verb.
questions.subject: upbo8-english

questions.question: Listen! Someone ______ at the door right now.

options.explanation: Simple Present is incorrect for actions happening now.
Past tense is incorrect for actions happening now.
Correct Present Continuous form.
Future tense is incorrect for actions happening now.

questions.explanation: The phrase 'right now' and the imperative 'Listen!' indicate an action happening at the moment of speaking, which requires the Present Continuous Tense.
questions.hint: Use the verb form that describes an action happening now.
questions.subject: upbo8-english

questions.question: I ______ my lunch, so I am not hungry anymore.

options.explanation: Simple Present is incorrect for completed actions.
Simple Past does not connect to present result.
Correct Present Perfect form.
Future tense is incorrect for completed actions.

questions.explanation: The action of eating lunch is completed, and its result (not being hungry) has a direct relevance to the present moment. This requires the Present Perfect Tense.
questions.hint: Use the verb form that connects past action to present result.
questions.subject: upbo8-english

questions.question: While my mother ______ in the garden, it suddenly started to rain.

options.explanation: Simple Present is incorrect for past actions.
Simple Past is incorrect for ongoing past actions.
Correct Past Continuous form.
Present Perfect is incorrect for past actions.

questions.explanation: The action of working was ongoing in the past when another past action (it started to rain) interrupted it. This situation is expressed using the Past Continuous Tense.
questions.hint: Use the verb form that describes an ongoing past action.
questions.subject: upbo8-english

questions.question: Don't disturb me between 7 PM and 8 PM tomorrow. I ______ my online class then.

options.explanation: Simple Present is incorrect for future actions.
Past tense is incorrect for future actions.
Simple Future is incorrect for ongoing future actions.
Correct Future Continuous form.

questions.explanation: The specific time frame 'between 7 PM and 8 PM tomorrow' indicates an action that will be in progress at a particular time in the future, requiring the Future Continuous Tense.
questions.hint: Use the verb form that describes an ongoing action at a specific future time.
questions.subject: upbo8-english

questions.question: Identify the sentence that correctly uses the Simple Present Tense in the 'if' clause of a Type 1 Conditional sentence.

options.text: If you will study hard, you will pass the exam.
options.explanation: Future tense in 'if' clause is incorrect for Type 1 Conditional.

options.text: If you studied hard, you would pass the exam.
options.explanation: Past tense in 'if' clause is incorrect for Type 1 Conditional.

options.text: If you study hard, you will pass the exam.
options.explanation: Correct use of Simple Present in 'if' clause and Simple Future in main clause.

options.text: If you study hard, you pass the exam.
options.explanation: Main clause lacks Simple Future tense.

questions.explanation: In a Type 1 Conditional sentence, the 'if' clause (condition) uses the Simple Present Tense, and the main clause (result) uses the Simple Future Tense.
questions.hint: Use Simple Present in the 'if' clause and Simple Future in the main clause.
questions.subject: upbo8-english

questions.question: She ______ for three hours when her father finally arrived home.

options.explanation: Simple Present is incorrect for past actions.
Past Continuous does not emphasize duration before another past action.
Present Perfect Continuous is incorrect for past actions.
Correct Past Perfect Continuous form.

questions.explanation: The action of sleeping was ongoing for a specified duration ('for three hours') and completed before another past action ('her father arrived home'). This describes a Past Perfect Continuous Tense situation.
questions.hint: Use the verb form that describes an action that was ongoing before another past action.
questions.subject: upbo8-english

questions.question: By the time the fire brigade arrived, the building ______ completely ______.

options.explanation: Present Perfect is incorrect for past actions.
Past Continuous does not emphasize completion before another past action.
Correct Past Perfect form.
Future tense is incorrect for past actions.

questions.explanation: The burning of the building happened and completed before another past action (the fire brigade arrived). To show the earlier past action, we use the Past Perfect Tense.
questions.hint: Use the verb form that describes an action completed before another past action.
questions.subject: upbo8-english

questions.question: The Earth ______ around the sun.

options.explanation: The base form 'revolve' is incorrect for a singular subject in the simple present tense.
The present continuous tense is not used for universal truths.
Correct! The simple present tense 'revolves' is used for a singular subject describing a universal truth.
The simple past tense 'revolved' is incorrect as it does not describe a current fact.

questions.explanation: This describes a universal truth or a scientific fact, which requires the simple present tense. For a singular subject ('The Earth'), the verb takes '-s' or '-es'.
questions.hint: Use the simple present tense for habitual or universal truths.
questions.subject: upbo8-english

questions.question: My grandmother ______ a beautiful story last night.

options.explanation: The simple present tense 'tells' is incorrect for a past action.
The present continuous tense 'is telling' is incorrect for a past action.
Correct! The simple past tense 'told' is used for a completed past action.
The future tense 'will tell' is incorrect for a past action.

questions.explanation: The phrase 'last night' indicates a completed action in the past, requiring the simple past tense of 'tell', which is 'told'.
questions.hint: Use the simple past tense for actions completed in the past.
questions.subject: upbo8-english

questions.question: We ______ to visit the zoo next Sunday.

options.explanation: The simple present tense 'plan' is incorrect for a future plan.
The simple past tense 'planned' is incorrect for a future action.
The future tense 'will plan' is less definite compared to 'are planning'.
Correct! The present continuous tense 'are planning' is used for a definite future plan.

questions.explanation: 'Next Sunday' indicates a definite future plan or arrangement, which is often expressed using the present continuous tense. While 'will plan' is also future, 'are planning' implies a more definite, pre-arranged event.
questions.hint: Use the present continuous tense for definite future plans.
questions.subject: upbo8-english

questions.question: Which of the following sentences uses the simple present tense correctly for a habitual action?

options.text: She is going to school every day.
options.explanation: The present continuous tense 'is going' is incorrect for a habitual action.

options.text: She goes to school every day.
options.explanation: Correct! The simple present tense 'goes' is used for a habitual action.

options.text: She went to school every day.
options.explanation: The simple past tense 'went' is incorrect for a habitual action.

options.text: She will go to school every day.
options.explanation: The future tense 'will go' is incorrect for a habitual action.

questions.explanation: 'Every day' signifies a habitual action, which is correctly expressed using the simple present tense. For a singular subject ('She'), the verb takes '-es'.
questions.hint: Habitual actions are expressed in the simple present tense.
questions.subject: upbo8-english

questions.question: Please be quiet! The baby ______ in the next room.

options.explanation: The simple present tense 'sleeps' is incorrect for an action happening now.
The simple past tense 'slept' is incorrect for an action happening now.
Correct! The present continuous tense 'is sleeping' is used for an action happening now.
The future tense 'will sleep' is incorrect for an action happening now.

questions.explanation: The command 'Please be quiet!' indicates that an action is happening at the moment of speaking, requiring the present continuous tense (is/am/are + verb-ing).
questions.hint: Use the present continuous tense for actions happening at the moment.
questions.subject: upbo8-english

questions.question: When the guests ______, we ______ dinner.

options.explanation: Correct! 'Arrived' (simple past) for the first action and 'were having' (past continuous) for the second action.
Incorrect structure for the second blank.
Incorrect tenses for past actions.
Incorrect structure for the second blank.

questions.explanation: This sentence describes two past actions. The first blank describes a completed action that happened at a specific point in the past (simple past). The second blank describes an ongoing action in the past that was in progress when the first action occurred (past continuous).
questions.hint: Use the simple past tense for the first action and the past continuous tense for the second action.
questions.subject: upbo8-english

questions.question: Identify the part of the sentence that has a grammatical error related to tense or subject-verb agreement: My brother / have been living / in Mumbai / for five years.

options.explanation: The subject 'My brother' is correct.
Correct! The error is in the auxiliary verb 'have' which should be 'has' for a singular subject.
This part of the sentence is grammatically correct.
This part of the sentence is grammatically correct.

questions.explanation: The subject 'My brother' is singular. Therefore, the auxiliary verb should be 'has' (for singular subjects) instead of 'have' (for plural subjects) in the present perfect continuous tense. It should be 'has been living'.
questions.hint: Check subject-verb agreement for singular and plural subjects.
questions.subject: upbo8-english

questions.question: Usually, birds ______ nests in spring, and this year, they ______ their new nest already.

options.explanation: Incorrect tense for the second blank.
Correct! 'Build' (simple present) for the first blank and 'have built' (present perfect) for the second blank.
Incorrect tenses for the given context.
Incorrect tenses for the given context.

questions.explanation: The first part describes a general or habitual action ('Usually'), requiring the simple present tense. The second part describes an action completed in the recent past with relevance to the present ('already'), requiring the present perfect tense.
questions.hint: Use the simple present tense for habitual actions and the present perfect tense for completed actions with present relevance.
questions.subject: upbo8-english

questions.question: By the time the fire brigade ______, the entire building ______ to ashes.

options.explanation: Incorrect tense for the first blank.
Correct! 'Arrived' (simple past) for the first blank and 'had burnt' (past perfect) for the second blank.
Incorrect tenses for past actions.
Incorrect structure for the first blank.

questions.explanation: This sentence describes two actions in the past, where one action was completed before the other. The action that happened earlier (building burning) requires the past perfect tense ('had burnt'), and the later action (fire brigade arriving) requires the simple past tense.
questions.hint: Use the past perfect tense for the action that happened earlier and the simple past tense for the later action.
questions.subject: upbo8-english

questions.question: If I ______ a millionaire, I ______ travel the world.

options.explanation: Incorrect verb forms for a second conditional sentence.
Incorrect verb forms for a second conditional sentence.
Correct! 'Were' (for all subjects in second conditional) and 'would travel' (main clause) are used.
Incorrect verb form in the main clause.

questions.explanation: This is a second conditional sentence, used to express an unreal or hypothetical situation in the present or future. In the 'if' clause for such conditions, 'were' is used for all subjects (even singular 'I'), and in the main clause, 'would + base form of verb' is used.
questions.hint: Use 'were' in the 'if' clause and 'would' in the main clause for second conditional sentences.
questions.subject: upbo8-english

questions.question: The sun ____ in the east.

options.explanation: Incorrect because 'rise' is the base form and does not agree with the singular subject 'the sun'.
Incorrect because 'rose' is the past tense and does not fit the context of a universal truth.
Correct because 'rises' is the Simple Present tense form for the singular subject 'the sun'.
Incorrect because the continuous form is not used for general truths.

questions.explanation: This sentence expresses a universal truth, which always uses the Simple Present tense.
questions.hint: Use the base form of the verb for general truths.
questions.subject: upbo8-english

questions.question: Yesterday, my mother ____ a delicious cake for my birthday.

options.explanation: Incorrect because 'bake' is the base form and does not indicate past action.
Incorrect because 'bakes' is the Simple Present tense and does not fit the past context.
Correct because 'baked' is the Simple Past tense form indicating a completed action.
Incorrect because the continuous form does not indicate a completed action.

questions.explanation: The word 'Yesterday' indicates a completed action in the past, requiring the Simple Past tense.
questions.hint: Use the past form of the verb to indicate a completed action.
questions.subject: upbo8-english

questions.question: She ____ for two hours now, and she's still not finished with her homework.

options.explanation: Correct because 'has been studying' is the Present Perfect Continuous tense, indicating an ongoing action.
Incorrect because 'is studying' does not indicate the duration of the action.
Incorrect because 'studied' is the Simple Past tense and does not indicate continuity.
Incorrect because 'will study' refers to a future action, not a present one.

questions.explanation: The phrase 'for two hours now' indicates an action that started in the past and is continuing up to the present moment. This is the correct usage of the Present Perfect Continuous tense.
questions.hint: Use a tense that shows an action continuing from the past to the present.
questions.subject: upbo8-english

questions.question: While I ____ my favourite book, my brother ____ into the room.

options.explanation: Incorrect because 'read' is Simple Past and does not indicate an ongoing action.
Correct because 'was reading' is Past Continuous (ongoing action) and 'walked' is Simple Past (interrupting action).
Incorrect because the sentence is in the past tense context.
Incorrect because the sentence requires past tense forms.

questions.explanation: The Past Continuous tense ('was reading') describes an ongoing action in the past, while the Simple Past tense ('walked') describes a sudden, interrupting action that occurred during the ongoing one.
questions.hint: Use the Past Continuous for the ongoing action and Simple Past for the interrupting action.
questions.subject: upbo8-english

questions.question: By the time you arrive tomorrow, we ____ all the preparations for the party.

options.explanation: Incorrect because 'will make' does not indicate completion before a specific future time.
Incorrect because 'will be making' indicates an ongoing action, not completion.
Correct because 'will have made' is the Future Perfect tense, indicating completion before a specific future time.
Incorrect because 'are making' is present continuous and does not fit the future context.

questions.explanation: The phrase 'By the time you arrive tomorrow' indicates a specific point in the future by which an action will be completed. This requires the Future Perfect tense ('will have made').
questions.hint: Use a tense that indicates an action completed before a specific future time.
questions.subject: upbo8-english
